title: Reading Values off a Three-Piece Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Define $h(x)=2x$ for $x\le 1$, $h(x)=3-x$ for $1<x\le 3$, and $h(x)=0$ for $x>3$. Compute $h(1)$, $h(2)$ and $h(4)$.

steps.title: Evaluate at the Boundary x=1
steps.explanation: The first branch carries the equality $x\\le 1$, so $x=1$ uses $2x$ and gives $2$.
steps.why: Boundary inputs go to the branch whose inequality includes them.

steps.title: Evaluate in the Middle Interval
steps.explanation: The input $2$ satisfies the middle condition $1<x\\le 3$, whose rule is $3-x$.
steps.why: Interior points select their branch by simple interval membership.

steps.title: Evaluate in the Tail Branch
steps.explanation: Inputs beyond $3$ hit the constant branch, so $h(4)=0$ regardless of the size of $4$.
steps.why: Constant pieces assign the same output to the entire tail of the domain.
